title: Tinsmith work on the cathedral and Jesuit church
summary: Interviewers show photos of New Orleans churches; Picou says he worked in and out on the cathedral spires and slating, and on the Jesuit church domes, as a tinsmith.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We wanted to talk a little bit about the scrapbook, if your daughter can find that scrapbook, to see what's in there, if there's some pictures or any... Yeah, oh yeah, she can find it. I know that. We wanted to talk to you a little bit of some other material about your life for Tulane University too. Yeah. And I think we got most of the facts about your life just when you were born and the early bands you played in the other time we talked to you about two years ago. So there may be a few other questions we were going to ask. Here's one thing, I brought these pictures of these churches. I wonder, you said you worked on the cathedral as a tin smith. Yeah. Do you remember what part you worked on? Was it the towers up there or the steeple? Those are pictures of the cathedral here. Yeah, I see. Opposite to Jackson Square. Yes, right to Jackson Square.
Did you work inside or outside? Was it inside the building?
Both. In and out. Both in and out.
On the steeples here? Yeah. On these spires? Sure. Oh yeah? What did you have to do there? Do some slating.
Oh, the slates. Oh, I see. You put in those things that hold the slates up? Yeah, yeah. I see, yeah. What do you call those? I know what you mean. They stop the slates from sliding down.

I know it's a groove. It's a groove. I know that. Okay. Okay, don't stop the gist. So long I have to do that. Did you have a shop someplace? Yeah. Was that at your home or did you have another shop someplace? Yeah, a shop, yeah. Yeah. Well, here's another church here, the Jesuit church over on Barone Street. Yeah. At one time, here's an old postcard of it. They didn't have the tower. Remember that one, right? Yeah. And then these big, they look like copper domes or something. Yeah. Oh Lord. Did you work on those too then? I know that thing so good. I've been too old. Can't go down here.
Did you ever work on these churches at the top? Oh sure.
Oh, you did. On the Jesuit church there too.

I wondered if you did any work on these domes up there. Yeah. The copper or brass. That's where you got your finger then. Right up on that dome. Yes indeed. You used to have to go up there? Yeah. That's pretty high. Yeah. I didn't mind that. You didn't mind climbing around, huh? No.
What did you do inside the church?
Oh, a different kind of work. On the walls, on the ceiling? Oh, a wall, yeah.
And ceiling, yeah. That was your trade, was it?
Tinsmith? Yeah. Tinsmith. Yeah. What does that cover?
Just all kinds of metal work? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. You were telling us once this building had been... You had to put it right... Outdoors there for a while.
